subject: Hospitality
title: The Birth of the Grand Hotel
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Birth of the Grand Hotel.

hook.text: In 1834, the first purpose-built luxury hotel opened in Hamburg—it wasn't converted from anything. It was designed to impress.

buildup.text: Grand hotels offered uniformed staff, fine dining, ballrooms, and reading rooms. They were palaces for paying guests.

discovery.text: They served a new class: wealthy industrial travelers who wanted luxury but didn't have aristocratic friends to host them.

twist.text: Grand hotels were among the first buildings with elevators, electric lights, and telephones. They were tech showrooms.

climax.text: The Savoy, the Ritz, the Waldorf—these hotels became as famous as the cities they stood in.

punchline.text: Not just lodging but spectacle. Grand hotels sold a dream.

quiz.question: What new class did grand hotels serve?
options: Wealthy industrial travelers without aristocratic connections
